stem.en: Scientists in India and in Japan study the same newly discovered insect. How does biological classification help them?

text.en: It stops the insect from ever becoming extinct in the wild.

feedback.en: Classification can show that a species is under threat, but it cannot stop extinction by itself.

text.en: It gives them one common system to identify and name it.

feedback.en: Right. Identifying and naming new organisms, in a system used worldwide, are two uses of classification.

text.en: It proves that the insect is useful to farmers and to crops.

feedback.en: Classification shows what an organism is related to. It does not decide whether it helps people.

text.en: It tells them the exact number of these insects still alive.

feedback.en: A count comes from a survey. Classification groups organisms; it does not count them.

explanation.en: Biological classification helps scientists identify and name newly discovered organisms, and it lets scientists all over the world discuss organisms using a common system.

hints.en: Think about what two scientists in different countries need in order to talk about one insect.

flags: Recap question added in the review/recap authoring pass; counterfactual-style question (what if the record used species names instead of a broad label). Not in the original outline. Standalone slide, no simulation.
